Hi Sanjay — thanks for the sheet. Looping in Rishi (infra) and Priyom (product) to validate. Below are concise answers we’ll consolidate into a single PDF and dataflow diagram for your packet.

1) Region pinning / residency\- Short answer: Yes, for customer payloads (non-PII application data) we support region pinning to a single cloud region (US only) on our Hosted API. This is enforced at the tenant routing layer and verified by our placement service.

2) Data categories & default retention\- Customer payloads (text inputs, generated output): default retention is 30 days in primary storage for troubleshooting and short-term cache; customers may request shorter retention via contract.
- KV/prefix cache: ephemeral, retained for up to 1 hour by default (configurable).
- Audit logs (operational metadata, request traces): 90 days by default for Hosted customers; extended retention available as an add-on.

3) Deletion & erasure process\- We provide a documented erasure API and workstream:
- Customer submits an erasure request via Console or API.
- Background job schedules deletion across caches + object stores; distributed tombstones applied; our orchestration verifies deletion and produces an erasure report (timestamped).
- Typical SLA for deletion completion: up to 14 days to reach all backups/replicas and internal indexes; most objects removed within 72 hours, and you’ll receive a deletion confirmation artifact.

4) Proof & evidence\- We can provide: deletion report (JSON/PDF), hash manifest of removed blobs, and an audit log excerpt (redacted) showing the erasure workflow execution. For compliance reviews we supply these artifacts as attachments.

5) Backups & cold storage\- Backups are retained for disaster recovery. For Hosted customers electing US-only residency, backups are stored in US regions only. Backup retention windows vary by plan; standard Hosted backup retention is 90 days — we can shorten by agreement.

6) Data exports & portability\- Customers can export tenant data via Console or the export API. Exports include payloads and metadata; we support CSV/JSON bundles and S3-compatible transfer.

We’ll produce a single PDF with the question-by-question responses and attach a simple region/dataflow diagram showing where tenant data, caches, logs, and backups live.

Attaching draft items for internal review: lynx_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (orig).

Thanks — we’ll push the final packet by EOD Thursday.

— Kimberly Park

- For the 14-day deletion SLA: does that include deletion from immutable backups? If not, what is your process for backup removal and how do you provide attestation?
- On region pinning: can you confirm that control plane metadata (tenant IDs, billing records) is also stored in the US only for pinned tenants, or is that cross-region? We need control-plane metadata residency for PCI/SOC considerations.

One more ask: procurement would like the deletion confirmation to include a timestamp and masking of any internal operator IDs.

Thanks — if you can call these out explicitly in the PDF, we’ll be good to proceed.

Sanjay — good questions. Final PDF attached (Lynx_HostedAPI_Answers_20261105.pdf) plus a region/dataflow figure (dataflow_hostedapi_region_map.png). Key clarifications below so procurement / security have explicit language to include in their packet: 

- Immutable backups: our standard immutable backup window depends on plan; deletion of customer data from active stores does not by itself remove immutable backups. For Hosted customers requesting full erasure including backups, we perform a restoration-and-delete workflow for affected objects and record the actions in an attestation artifact. We commit to providing a backup removal attestation within 30 days of an approved erasure order for standard Hosted plans; shorter timelines can be contractually agreed for enterprise contracts.

- Control plane metadata residency: For tenants that opt into US-only residency, all tenant identifiers, minimal billing metadata, and routing metadata are stored in the selected US control-plane region. Aggregated telemetry (anonymized operational metrics) may cross regions for monitoring; we do not store raw customer payloads outside the pinned region.

- Deletion confirmation contents: the erasure report we send contains: timestamp (ISO 8601), list of resources removed (redacted identifiers), and workflow run id. Operator/user IDs are masked in shared artifacts; full operator audit trails are available to the customer under NDA for legal review.
